_: The sentences that make claude claude, and the one place they are written.
Excising these is what makes room for a different identity instead of a
second one arguing with the first.
min_system_chars is the line between a prompt worth judging and one that is
not, and it is measured rather than guessed. Claude Code's agent prompt was
12,066 chars on v2.1.220. It also makes smaller requests with system prompts
of their own - a title generation, a quota probe - which contain some of
these sentences and not others, and judging one of those reported a failed
excision on a rewrite that was working. That false alarm is the exact thing
this file exists to avoid, so the threshold sits above the largest of them
(~5,300 chars) and well below the agent prompt. The residual risk is the
quiet direction: if the agent prompt ever shrinks past this, we stop
judging rather than start lying.
They are pinned to exact sentences of a particular Claude Code release, and
a future one that rewords its opening line will match none of them. That is
the failure this file exists to make loud: a miss on a real system prompt is
recorded in the usage log, marked on the status line, and reported by
`bottleneck kernel`, because the alternative is a session that looks fine
and quietly carries two identities.
pattern  the regex excised from every system text block
witness  a plain substring of what it removes. Checked after the rewrite:
still present means the excision did not do its job, which is what
a partly reworded sentence looks like - the pattern matches some of
it and leaves the rest behind, so counting matches alone says fine
matched  the Claude Code version the pattern was last confirmed against

excise.name: cli-sentence
excise.pattern: You are Claude Code, Anthropic's official CLI for Claude\.\s*

excise.name: interactive-agent
excise.pattern: You are an interactive agent that helps users with software engineering tasks\.\s*
excise.witness: interactive agent that helps users with software engineering
